digest.component_or_area: autodeploy timer and docker garbage collection
propositions: During main branch quiescence, the no-op early exit at autodeploy.sh:228 returns without invoking docker garbage collection, causing root disk to accumulate and remain in ALARM state between deploys.

The prune_docker_caches() function is defined after line 228 (at autodeploy.sh:245), preventing its use on the no-op path without first relocating the function definition above line 150 into the helper block where it will precede all call sites.

Adding a pressure-triggered, throttled reclaim to the no-op path requires new tunables (DISK_PRESSURE_PCT, PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL, PRESSURE_PRUNE_TS_FILE) and helper functions (root_disk_pct, reclaim_under_pressure) to conditionally invoke docker prune when root usage exceeds threshold and minimum interval has elapsed.

The reclaim_under_pressure() helper must use atomic file operations to persist the last-prune timestamp, enforce a flat-floor absolute threshold rather than derivative-based logic, and emit a countable AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE journal marker on each triggered prune.
A docker prune failure on the pressure path must not alter the script's overall exit code and must only emit a log message, consistent with deploy-path prune guarantees.

New test module test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py must verify prune invocation above threshold, throttle suppression, below-threshold no-op, failure non-fatality, and correct marker emission via stubbed df and docker shims.
